draft_quotes: The appellate record concerns an application under Section 8 of the U.P. Debt Redemption Act (No. XIII of 1940) filed by five judgment-debtors to amend a decree passed in O.S. No. 33 of 1938 [Sa0cc2677dff8].

The underlying debt originated from a mortgage deed executed on June 22, 1922, by Madho Ram, Sita Ram, Jai Ram, and Lakshman in favour of Damodarji for Rs. 8,000 at 12 annas per cent per mensem [Sf6ab759d9134].

On July 28, 1931, these mortgagors and their sons executed a fresh mortgage over the same properties in favour of Kothi Kamta Nathji Vishwanathji for Rs. 3,000, reciting that Rs. 8,000 was advanced by cheque to pay off the earlier 1922 debt [S5c8b7a555503].

In the original suit filed in 1938, the plaintiffs argued that the mortgagors were not "agriculturists" under the U.P. Agriculturists' Relief Act because Sita Ram was assessed to income tax [S3dcbf8433ad4].

The Trial Court held that Sita Ram's tax liability did not exceed the cess payable on his land, thus qualifying him as an agriculturist, and scaled down interest to pass a preliminary decree for Rs. 9,497-14-1 [S2fbf3e5eb127][S15b6886f8dbb].

Following the enactment of the U.P. Debt Redemption Act in 1940, the judgment-debtors applied in April 1942 for relief, asserting that the actual advance occurred in 1922 and requesting that accounts be reopened from that date to show full discharge of the debt [S95aee3f2145e].

The decree-holders objected, arguing that the petitioners were members of a joint Hindu family, that Sita Ram paid income tax at the time of the 1931 mortgage and the 1942 application, and that the 1931 transaction was not a "loan" within the meaning of the Act [S1b8a01394a3c][Saee84f81cd7f].
However, the record notes that the decree-holders did not contest the specific prayer to take accounts from 1922 [Se54d7d19029a].

Evidence was led showing Sita Ram earned Rs. 90 per month in 1930 and 1931 with no income tax deducted until February 1932; the assessment form dated February 9, 1933, covered the year 1931-32 [S0352dfc9457d][S3c4a5a9113b1][S0fd10e2fb41a]. No rebutting evidence was adduced by the decree-holders [S0fd10e2fb41a].

The Additional Civil Judge found that Sita Ram was not assessed to income tax at the date of the 1931 mortgage or the 1942 application, holding the applicants qualified as agriculturists and the transaction constituted a "loan" [S9adf66efbf95].

Addressing the scope of accounting, the Judge determined that the mortgagees in the 1922 and 1931 deeds were effectively the same entity and, relying on evidence from the 1938 suit and noting the decree-holders' failure to produce account books, reopened the accounts from June 2, 1922 [S7ad75b5a8d65][S111ddbfcfbeb]. He concluded that the entire principal and interest had been discharged, declaring the decree fully satisfied [Sfa55b32acae2].

On appeal, the High Court Division Bench dismissed the decree-holders' challenge regarding the "agriculturist" status. It held that under Section 21 of the Act, recovery was limited to the mortgaged property, rendering the proviso to the definition of "loan" (which requires the borrower to be an agriculturist at the time of advance) inapplicable [S98c21090d1c5]. Since it was undisputed that the judgment-debtors were agriculturists at the date of the suit, the case fell within the precedent of *Ketki Kunwar v. Ram Saroop* [Sdb081d7e6939][Sb6f4e643830c].

Crucially, the High Court noted that the question of whether accounts should be reopened from 1922 or 1931 was not raised by the decree-holders in that appeal [Sb6f4e643830c]. The matter now reaches the Supreme Court via certificate under Section 110 of the Code of Civil Procedure [Sb6f4e643830c].

The statutory framework defines a "loan" as an advance made before June 1, 1940, recoverable from an agriculturist, provided the advance was made to an agriculturist [L81efa2890bf4][Sff81fb3988bd]. An "agriculturist" is defined as a proprietor or tenant, excluding those assessed to income tax unless specific provisos apply [L81efa2890bf4].

unresolved: The Supreme Court's final ruling on whether accounts should be reopened from 1922 or 1931.
Whether the Supreme Court accepted the lower courts' reliance on the 1938 suit evidence for the 1942 application.
The specific impact of the decree-holders' failure to produce books of account on the burden of proof in the Supreme Court.
